kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the three printed blocks — 4 patterns (the opioid pinpoint-pupil stem, the anticholinergic dilated-pupil toxidrome, the inducer-causes-therapeutic-failure stem on warfarin/OCP/theophylline/anti-epileptics, the inhibitor-causes-toxicity stem), 4 traps (meperidine vs every other opioid, chronic vs acute alcohol direction, grapefruit juice vs St. John's wort as the two non-drug agents, sulfonamide antibiotics vs the non-antibiotic sulfa family), 3 pivots (the two-muscle pupil router, the CYP direction-first rule, the sulfa-family check), and 8 recall cards covering all three blocks verbatim.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the three blocks' lists only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the reading protocols are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two KYP reading protocols: (1) the IRIS TWO-PULL rule — RADIAL OPENS (α1 driven by direct/indirect sympathomimetics, or unopposed when anticholinergics block M3) vs SPHINCTER CLOSES (M3 driven by parasympathomimetics/organophosphates, or won by default when sympatholytics withdraw the α1 pull or opioids act centrally), with meperidine as the printed exception on both sides; (2) the CYP ENZYME-AMPLITUDE rule — induce = more enzyme = less drug = therapeutic failure, inhibit = less enzyme = more drug = toxicity, with the four substrate gauges (INR, theophylline, OCP efficacy, seizure control) and the chronic-vs-acute alcohol two-direction quirk.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the pupil block as two flat drug columns and the CYP block as three flat name lists; it never asks the learner to route each drug through the muscle it moves or to file each interaction by direction before naming the consequence. Both protocols, the two mechanism flows, and the four-moves CYP steps are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] + mechanisms[1] + blocks[2] the two-pull compare + blocks[4] the four-moves steps + the registry visual's Zones A/B and protocol strip

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (RADIAL OPENS, SPHINCTER CLOSES / EVERY OPIOID PINPOINTS — EXCEPT MEPERIDINE / MORE ENZYME, LESS DRUG / SULFA IS A FAMILY, NOT A DRUG). First Aid's own mnemonics — 'St. John's funny funny (phen-phen) mom never refuses greasy carbs and chronic alcohol' (inducers), 'The OCPs are anti-war' (substrates), 'SICK FACES come when I am really drinking grapefruit juice' (inhibitors), all three printing INSIDE the CYP table in a red bottom row, and 'Scary Sulfa Pharm FACTS' printing in red in the right margin — are carried ATTRIBUTED inside the verbatim carries, the memory callout, and the visual, and are NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source's own mnemonics are preserved and attributed; the four ALL-CAPS codes that organize the page's logic (two-pull, opioid exception, CYP direction, sulfa family) are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[8] the memory callout + the visual's mnemonic bands

kypExtensions.summary: The warfarin + trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole miniCase — a stable-INR patient whose INR climbs to 9.4 five days after starting TMP-SMX — with the correct answer routing two printed rows (warfarin substrate + sulfonamides inhibitor = less enzyme, more drug) and distractors inverting the direction (induction), borrowing the wrong block (the IgE sulfa-allergy story from the page's third block), and reaching for the non-printed gut-flora/vitamin-K mechanism; the vignette, the four options, and the reasoning are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the substrate and inhibitor lists separately and never intersects them in a clinical vignette; the case is KYP's synthesis and dissection.

kypExtensions.summary: The four DrugCards (meperidine — the pupil-dilating opioid exception; rifampin — the prototype inducer; cimetidine — the prototype inhibitor; sulfonamide antibiotics — the sulfa-family anchor), one per testable individual spanning all three blocks; each card's fields are explicitly marked where they are KYP context rather than printed text (the page prints only the pupil lists, the CYP name lists, and the sulfa block — no mechanisms, no uses, no adverse effects for these drugs).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source organizes its pharmacology as class lists and interaction tables, not as drug cards; the card layer is a KYP presentation, and every non-printed statement on the cards is flagged as KYP context.
